Perfect! I now have a clear picture of the issue. Looking at the pod information from earlier, the current job has `activeDeadlineSeconds: null`, which means there is NO timeout set. The job is hung downloading a file and will continue running indefinitely, blocking all subsequent CronJob executions due to the `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` setting.

Based on my investigation:
- The stock-sync job started at 14:15 on 2026-05-21 and is still running after 19+ hours
- It got stuck during a large file download (11.2 MB / 38.4 MB)
- The job has no `activeDeadlineSeconds` timeout configured, so it runs indefinitely
- The CronJob has `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`, which prevents new jobs from starting while the previous one is running
- All subsequent scheduled runs (every 15 minutes) have been skipped since the job hung

The fix is to delete the stuck pod, which will allow the next scheduled CronJob execution to proceed. Let me update the ticket with this resolution.

input.note:
**Cause**: The stock-sync job pod (stock-sync-29656215-wq7fz) started at 2026-05-21T14:15:01Z and became hung during a large file download (11.2 MB / 38.4 MB), running for 19+ hours. The pod has no activeDeadlineSeconds timeout configured, so it continues indefinitely.

**Evidence**: 
- Pod logs show the job stalled at "11.2 MB / 38.4 MB" starting at 2026-05-21T14:16:02Z and never progressed
- The CronJob is configured with `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs#job-creation-2], which blocks new job executions while the previous one is running
- According to Kubernetes documentation, long-running jobs with concurrencyPolicy:Forbid cause scheduled times to be skipped until the previous job completes [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs#job-creation-1]
- The job has `activeDeadlineSeconds: null`, meaning no timeout is enforced [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/job#job-termination-and-cleanup-1]

**Fix**: Delete the stuck pod to allow the next scheduled CronJob execution to proceed:
```
kubectl delete pod stock-sync-29656215-wq7fz -n warehouse
```

This will terminate the hung job and allow the CronJob to execute normally on the next schedule. Consider also adding an `activeDeadlineSeconds` to the CronJob spec to prevent similar hangs in the future (e.g., 900 seconds for a job that typically completes in 3-4 minutes).
